tasks.title: Main and bridge: declare the pod:commands invoke channel, answer it from each session's slash-command state, and forward it through the preload bridge
acceptance: C1. `src/shared/contracts/ipc.ts` adds exactly the two declarations `contracts/pod-commands-pull.ts` gives: `podCommands: 'pod:commands'` in `INVOKE_CHANNELS`, placed directly after `podFork` (`ipc.ts:104` at e7fed6b), and `commands(podId: PodId): Promise<IpcResult<SlashCommandInfo[]>>` in `OrcastrateApi['pods']`. The method's docblock restates that contract's answer rules (open Pod with a list, open Pod with no catalog yet, Pod with no live session), its three error codes, and that it resolves and never rejects. Evidence: a new test in `tests/unit/ipc/channels.test.ts` asserts `INVOKE_CHANNELS.podCommands` is `'pod:commands'`; it fails at e7fed6b, where the member is `undefined`. Control: `grep -c "podCommands: 'pod:commands'" /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261113-2303-pod-commands-pull/src/shared/contracts/ipc.ts` prints 1 (it printed 0 at e7fed6b, measured at authoring), and `PodCommandsPush` and `EVENT_CHANNELS` are byte-unchanged in the diff.

C2. The docblock of `PodCommandsPush` (`ipc.ts:329-334` at e7fed6b) keeps its three statements (whole snapshot, emit order per Pod, no revision) and adds the pull ordering rule stated in place: a renderer may also read the same list over `pod:commands`, and it drops a pull answer for a Pod if a push for that Pod arrived after the pull was sent. The reviewer reads the docblock; there is no instrument for this one.

C3. In `tests/unit/ipc/channels.test.ts`, the invoke-count test ('declares exactly 22 invoke channels', `:41-46` at e7fed6b) and the installed-count assertion (`:80`) assert 23, and the first test's name says 23. The push-count test (`:48-52`) still asserts 7. All pass.

C4. In `tests/unit/ipc/channels.test.ts`, the mapped-type guards `returnsAreClean` (`:293`) and `argumentsAreClean` (`:362`) gain `commands: true`, and `podReturningMethodsStillReturnPod` (`:315`) gains `commands: Exact<ValueOf<'commands'>, SlashCommandInfo[]>`. This is the existing openness prohibition applied to the new method (the `OrcastrateApi` docblock at `ipc.ts:352-394` at e7fed6b, 'no method here may ever carry a parallel openness field'). Evidence: `npm --prefix /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261113-2303-pod-commands-pull run typecheck:node` exits 0 (C14).

C5. The runtime openness sweep in `tests/unit/ipc/channels.test.ts` ('no reply on any frozen invoke channel carries an openness field', its `args` map at `:406`) gains `[INVOKE_CHANNELS.podCommands]: [podId]`, so the sweep receives an `ok: true` answer from `pod:commands` rather than skipping a failed envelope. The test asserts that this channel's result was `ok` (a vacuity guard for the new row), and passes.

C6a. `SlashCommandState` (`src/main/pod-manager/slash-commands.ts`) gains a public method `current(): SlashCommandInfo[] | undefined`, a method and not a public field (backend discipline, Layering: 'A module exposes behavior, not its internal state. Public mutable fields are not an interface.'). A new test in `tests/unit/pod-manager/slash-commands.test.ts` asserts that a fresh state answers `undefined`.
C6b. A new test asserts that after `acceptInitialRead` of a two-entry list, `current()` deep-equals the list that call returned.

C6c. A new test asserts that after an `init` whose `terminal_slash_commands` names one catalog entry, `current()` omits that entry and deep-equals the list the `observe` call returned. Shown able to fail by injecting, at the one return site of `current()`, a version that answers the unfiltered catalog (a copy of `#catalog`); name the file:line and the command run, and report the red result.
C6d. A new test asserts that when a mutator returns `null` because the visible list did not change, `current()` still deep-equals the previously reported list.
C6e. A new test asserts that after a `commands_changed` replaced the catalog, a late `acceptInitialRead` (which returns `null`) leaves `current()` equal to the `commands_changed` list.

C6f. A new test asserts that pushing an entry onto the array `current()` returned does not change what the next `current()` call returns. Shown able to fail by injecting a `current()` that returns `this.#lastReported` itself; report the site and the red result.

C7a. `PodManagerApi` (`pod-manager.ts:144-161` at e7fed6b) gains `listSlashCommands(podId: PodId): SlashCommandInfo[]`, synchronous, and `PodManager` implements it. It throws the same NOT_FOUND failure `listLanes` throws (`#requirePod`, `pod-manager.ts:1108-1111` and `:1639-1643` at e7fed6b) when there is no Pod row; otherwise it answers `current()` of the Pod's live session, or `[]` when there is no live session or `current()` is `undefined`. A new test file `tests/unit/pod-manager/slash-commands-pull.test.ts`, built on the same assembled-pipeline harness as `slash-commands-push.test.ts`, asserts that for an open Pod whose `supportedCommands` answered two commands, `listSlashCommands` deep-equals the `commands` of the last `push:podCommands` for that Pod.
C7b. A new test asserts that an open Pod whose `supportedCommands()` has not settled (a promise the test never resolves) answers `[]`.
C7c. A new test asserts that a Pod row that was never opened answers `[]`.

C7d. A new test asserts that a Pod that had a non-empty list answers `[]` after `closePod`. Shown able to fail by injecting a defect that lets a closed Pod answer its last list (name the site you chose, for example keeping the session in `#sessions` in `#dispose` at `pod-manager.ts:1013` at e7fed6b); report the site and the red result.
C7e. A new test asserts that after a close and a reopen, before the new session's read settles, the Pod answers `[]` (the list is per session, `pod-manager.ts:192-196` at e7fed6b).
C7f. A new test asserts that after an `init` naming one command in `terminal_slash_commands`, the answer omits it and deep-equals the last push.

C7g. A new test asserts that `listSlashCommands` for an id with no Pod row throws a failure whose code is `NOT_FOUND`. Shown able to fail by removing the `#requirePod` call from `listSlashCommands`; report the site and the red result.

C7h. A new test asserts that calling `listSlashCommands` on an open Pod with a list emits no push (the harness's pushed list is the same length before and after) and logs nothing (the injected `warn` and `error` spies are not called).

C8. `src/main/ipc/handlers.ts` registers `INVOKE_CHANNELS.podCommands` with a handler that does only `manager.listSlashCommands(requirePodId(podId))`, next to `pod:fork` (`handlers.ts:181` at e7fed6b). The file still contains no `opened` token, which the existing guard 'src/main/ipc validates no status and knows no openness field' in `channels.test.ts` checks.

C9a. A new test file `tests/unit/ipc/pod-commands.test.ts`, driven through the `makeHarness` IPC harness, asserts that `pod:commands` for an open Pod whose read answered resolves `{ ok: true }` whose value deep-equals the last `push:podCommands` commands for that Pod.
C9b. A new test asserts that `pod:commands` for a closed Pod resolves `{ ok: true, value: [] }`.

C9c. A new test asserts that `pod:commands` with `''` resolves `{ ok: false }` with code `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Shown able to fail by registering the handler without `requirePodId` (so `''` reaches the manager and answers NOT_FOUND); report the site and the red result.
C9d. A new test asserts that `pod:commands` with `42` resolves `{ ok: false }` with code `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
C9e. A new test asserts that `pod:commands` with an id no Pod has resolves `{ ok: false }` with code `NOT_FOUND`.

C10. `tests/unit/ipc/envelope.test.ts`: the `rigThatThrows` manager literal (`:143` at e7fed6b) gains `listSlashCommands: boom`; `VALID_ARGS` (`:45`) gains `[INVOKE_CHANNELS.podCommands]: ['p1']`; and `BAD_ARGS` (`:75`) gains `[INVOKE_CHANNELS.podCommands]: ['']`, or another malformed id. The existing per-channel sweeps then walk 23 channels and pass, including 'answers INVALID_ARGUMENT for malformed input on every handler that takes an argument' (`:273`) and 'answers INVALID_ARGUMENT when an argument is simply missing' (`:294`). `ZERO_ARG_CHANNELS` (`:101`) is unchanged.

C11a. `src/preload/api.ts` adds `commands: (podId: PodId) => call<SlashCommandInfo[]>(INVOKE_CHANNELS.podCommands, podId)` to `pods`. The `invoke channels` table in `src/preload/api.test.ts` (`:66-141` at e7fed6b) gains the row `['pods.commands', (a) => a.pods.commands('p'), INVOKE_CHANNELS.podCommands]`, and that row's generated test passes.

C11b. A new test in `src/preload/api.test.ts`, shaped like the `pods.fork` test at `:172-179` at e7fed6b, asserts `ipc.calls` equals `[{ channel: 'pod:commands', args: ['pod-7'] }]` after `api.pods.commands('pod-7')`. It fails at e7fed6b, where `api.pods.commands` is not a function.

C12. No file this task writes cites a session id or a `.sir/` path. `grep -rnE "\.sir/|[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{4}-[a-z]" /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261113-2303-pod-commands-pull/src/shared/contracts/ipc.ts /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261113-2303-pod-commands-pull/src/preload /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261113-2303-pod-commands-pull/src/main/pod-manager /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261113-2303-pod-commands-pull/src/main/ipc /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261113-2303-pod-commands-pull/tests/unit/ipc /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261113-2303-pod-commands-pull/tests/unit/pod-manager` prints nothing; it printed nothing at e7fed6b too (measured at authoring). Positive control: the same pattern over `src/renderer/src/__tests__/failure-paths.e2e.test.tsx` prints its line 29. Near-miss it is not meant to catch: the DIR-style id `2026-08-20-orcastrate-pod-lifecycle` at `ipc.ts:383`.

C13. `npm --prefix /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261113-2303-pod-commands-pull test -- tests/unit/ tests/router/ src/main/ src/preload/` exits 0, and its `Tests` line reports more than 1206 passed. At e7fed6b this command printed `Test Files 75 passed (75)` and `Tests 1206 passed (1206)` (measured at authoring; the 75 files were counted a second way with `find` over the same four directories). tasks.title: Renderer: pull each Pod's command list once at store start, keep a push that lands while the pull is in flight, and cover the pull in the stub, the failure sweep and an end-to-end reload test
acceptance: D1. `src/renderer/src/test-utils/stub-api.ts`: `INVOKE_CHANNEL_METHODS` (`:79-102` at e7fed6b) gains `podCommands: ['pods', 'commands']`. The stub's `pods` gains `commands: channel('podCommands', (_podId: PodId): SlashCommandInfo[] => [])`, so every call is recorded in `calls.podCommands`, `failInvoke('podCommands', ...)` applies to it, and `overrides.pods.commands` replaces it. In `stub-api.test.ts`, 'covers all 22 invoke channels' (`:69-71` at e7fed6b) asserts 23 and its name says 23. The existing walk ('maps every INVOKE_CHANNELS member to a stub method', `:59`) passes with the new member.

D2a. In `src/renderer/src/state/store.ts`, `start()` pulls once for each Pod returned by the first successful `pods.list` it issues. It does not move this into `refreshPods`, which other actions also call. A new test in `store.test.ts`, where `pods.list` answers `makeStubPods()`, asserts that once start's reads settle, `api.calls.podCommands` holds exactly one call for `pod-1` and one for `pod-2`, each with the bare id as its only argument. It fails at e7fed6b, where `calls.podCommands` does not exist.
D2b. A new test asserts that when `pods.list` fails during `start()`, `api.calls.podCommands` is empty once the store settles.

D3. A new test asserts that the pulls are issued together: with `pods.commands` overridden to return promises the test holds unresolved, both Pods' calls are recorded before either is resolved. This encodes frontend discipline, Data fetching: 'Requests whose results are independent are issued together.' The pulls wait on `pods.list` because they need its ids; a comment at the call site says so, which is the justification the same rule asks of a dependent chain. Shown able to fail by injecting a sequential `for ... await` over the Pods; report the site and the red result.

D4a. A new test asserts that after start settles, `setActivePod('pod-2')` then `setActivePod('pod-1')` leaves `calls.podCommands` at 2 calls. This encodes frontend discipline, Data fetching: 'Fetching belongs to an explicit lifecycle or event.' The lifecycle is `start()`, not a switch. Shown able to fail by injecting a pull into `setActivePod`; report the site and the red result.
D4b. A new test asserts that a later `actions.refreshPods()` call leaves `calls.podCommands` at 2. Shown able to fail by moving the pull into `refreshPods`; report the site and the red result.

D5. A new test asserts that a non-empty answer for `pod-2` becomes that Pod's list: `getState().runtimes['pod-2']?.slashCommands` is the very array the answer delivered (`toBe`). This matches the 'no copy' rule of the runtime field's docblock (`store.ts:123-130` at e7fed6b).

D6a. A new test asserts that an empty answer for a Pod whose list is already empty commits no state. `getState()` is the same object (`toBe`) immediately before and after that answer settles, with the answer held by the test so nothing else lands in between. Shown able to fail by injecting an unconditional `patchRuntime` write of the answer; report the site and the red result.
D6b. A new test asserts that an empty answer replaces a list that a push delivered before the pull was sent (emitted while `pods.list` was still in flight) with `NO_SLASH_COMMANDS` itself (`toBe`).

D7. THE RACE. A new test asserts that when a `podCommands` push for `pod-2` is emitted after the pull for `pod-2` was sent and before its answer settles, the Pod's list after the answer settles is the pushed array (`toBe`), not the answer. Shown able to fail by injecting the removal of the push-after-pull drop, so that the answer is applied unconditionally; report the site and the red result. This injection is required, not optional.

D8. A new test asserts that a push for `pod-2` emitted BEFORE its pull was sent (while `pods.list` is in flight) does not drop the answer: the answer is the list after it settles. Shown able to fail by injecting a drop for any push ever seen for that Pod; report the site and the red result.

D9. A new test asserts that a push for `pod-1` emitted while `pod-2`'s pull is in flight does not drop `pod-2`'s answer. Shown able to fail by injecting a single drop marker shared by all Pods; report the site and the red result.

D10. A new test asserts that a failed pull (`failInvoke('podCommands', ipcError('IO', ...))`, or a held answer resolving `{ ok: false }`) commits no state: `getState()` is the same object (`toBe`) immediately before and after the failed answer settles. Shown able to fail by injecting a write of the error into any state field on failure; report the site and the red result.

D11. In `store.test.ts`, the coverage test 'covers every invoke channel between the action table and the lifecycle reads' (`:321-333` at e7fed6b) adds `podCommands` to `covered`, with a comment that it is the startup lifecycle read and fails silently by design. The equality assertion is unchanged and passes.

D12a. In `src/renderer/src/__tests__/failure-paths.e2e.test.tsx`, `SURFACELESS_CHANNELS` (`:193` at e7fed6b) gains `'podCommands'`, and the comment above it says why: the pull is reached on every start and fails silently by design. `UNREACHABLE_CHANNELS` (`:206-209`) is unchanged. The classification sweep's generated row for `podCommands` passes, and that row asserts both `api.calls.podCommands.length > 0` (reachable, because `sweepApi` lists two Pods) and that its sentinel never appears on screen. Shown able to fail by injecting into `store.ts` a `start()` that issues no pull; report the site and the red result.

D12b. The count assertions in the same file (`:577-579` and `:628` at e7fed6b) become 23, 3 and 20. The surfaced-list equality (`:679-701`) still lists the same 20 names in the same order, and passes.

D12c. The same file's prose counts match the code. The header's arithmetic paragraph (`:22-26` at e7fed6b) says there are twenty-three invoke channels, twenty surface, and three do not: two because nothing calls them (`UNREACHABLE_CHANNELS`) and one, `podCommands`, because its failure is silent by design. The two sweep-cost comments (`:120-128`, `:134-139`) name the channel count the sweep actually runs, which is `INVOKE_KEYS.length`. Instrument: `grep -nE "TWENTY-TWO|twenty-one" /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261113-2303-pod-commands-pull/src/renderer/src/__tests__/failure-paths.e2e.test.tsx` prints nothing. At e7fed6b it printed 4 lines (22, 121, 135, 572; measured at authoring), and `twenty-one` was already stale there against 22 channels.

D13a. A new file `src/renderer/src/__tests__/pod-commands-pull.e2e.test.tsx` mounts the real workspace through `mountWorkspace` (as `slash-commands.e2e.test.tsx` does) over a stub whose `pods.list` answers one Pod with status `'idle'` and whose `pods.commands` answers two commands for it. The stub emits no `podCommands` push, and the test sends no turn. Typing `/` in the composer shows both command names in the suggestion list, in the answer's order, and `api.calls.podSend` is empty. This is the reload scenario: a fresh renderer, with main already holding the list. It fails at e7fed6b, where nothing fills the list without a push.

The docblocks that said the list arrives only by push say what is now true: a Pod's list comes from its pushes and from the one startup pull, a push that lands while the pull is in flight wins, and the hook itself still issues no IPC call. The sites are `renderer-state.ts:789-807`, `workspace-provider.tsx:60-65` and `:414-420`, `store.ts:123-130`, and the comment at `App.tsx:95-97` (all at e7fed6b). Control, preserved: `grep -rnE "\.sir/|[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{4}-[a-z]" /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261113-2303-pod-commands-pull/src /c/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261113-2303-pod-commands-pull/tests | wc -l` prints 7, exactly as at e7fed6b (measured at authoring).
